subject: Dedicated capacity: definitions, throughput floor & SLA credit triggers
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@luminadx.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@luminadx.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: throughput baseline & SLA credit trigger

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Lumina's engineering and ML teams are excited about the performance you showed. Before we move to an internal approval, procurement and legal have a couple of open items on the Dedicated (reserved pool) pricing/contract:

1) Definitions — we need clarity on what a "capacity unit" represents for billing and SLA measurement. Our finance team wants to map it back to a predictable metric (e.g., GPU-hour, or tokens/sec per GPU equivalent).
2) Throughput baseline — Lumina requires a throughput floor guarantee for steady-state inference (we typically run long-running inference bursts at night) and need to understand measurement windows and sampling.
3) SLA credits — Legal proposed a credit ladder tied to realized throughput vs committed throughput. We proposed the language below in our procurement template (attached).

Could you confirm how Redwood will define and measure the committed throughput, and whether you can accept a credit ladder starting at 95% realized-throughput for partial remediation? We attached our standard redlines for reference (Lumina_redlines_0319.docx).

Goal: get a clean set of definitions and a mutual action plan so procurement can sign off on the commercial term sheet next week.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Lumina Diagnostics

Attachment: Lumina_redlines_0319.docx (redline summary, 3 pages)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@luminadx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: throughput baseline & SLA credit trigger

Elena — thanks for the note and the redlines. High level response below; detailed proposal attached.

Short answers:
- Capacity unit: we propose "Committed Capacity Unit (CCU)" = 1 reserved GPU-hour within a contracted pooled bundle, measured at the runtime scheduler level and billed per hour. For cross-model parity we normalize to a gpt-4-family-equivalent GPU in our internal meter so customers can map costs across model families.
- Throughput measurement: we measure realized throughput as the 5-minute rolling average of successfully served tokens originating from a customer's tenancy, aggregated across the reserved pool, using the serving runtime logs. Measurement windows and sampling are included in the SLA doc.
- SLA credit ladder: we can accept a tiered credit ladder but need to align the trigger thresholds and remedy caps to avoid unbounded exposure on high-burst workloads. See the attached "proposed-commit-worksheet.xlsx" and a sample SLA redline for structure.

Attached: proposed-commit-worksheet.xlsx; sample-sla-redline.pdf

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood to send a short glossary (definitions + measurement method) by EOD Thu.
2) Lumina to provide target committed pool size (in CCUs) and expected nightly burst profile so we can validate the normalization.
3) Parallel legal redline pass — we can take Lumina's doc and respond to the specific credit percentages within 2 business days.

Looping Marissa (pricing lead) and Ben (customer success lead) for commercial and operational sizing support.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-commit-worksheet.xlsx, sample-sla-redline.pdf

From: Legal Team <legal@luminadx.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena@luminadx.com>, procurement@luminadx.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina redlines: throughput guarantee and credit ladder (follow-up)

Aditya / Redwood team,

Attaching our formal redline (Lumina_redlines_0319.docx). Key asks called out here:

- Throughput Guarantee: "Committed Throughput" should be defined as the median per-5-minute throughput across the contracted pool during a calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and agreed burst periods.
- Credit ladder: we propose: 5% service credit if realized throughput < 95% of committed; 15% if < 90%; 30% if < 80% (cumulative cap 60% per month).
- Measurement transparency: monthly measurement report and raw metrics exportable to Lumina for audit on request.

Please provide Redwood's position on each bullet. We appreciate specificity on the exact measurement query and any exclusions (e.g., model-specific warmup, KV cache priming).

Regards,
Lumina Legal

Attachment: Lumina_redlines_0319.docx (formal redline)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@luminadx.com>, legal@luminadx.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumina redlines: throughput guarantee and credit ladder (proposal)

Hi Elena / Lumina Legal — thanks for the clear redline. We reviewed internally (engineering + product + legal) and would like to propose a compromise that protects Lumina's operational needs while keeping the remedy exposure manageable for Redwood. Summary below; full glossary attached.

1) Definitions (proposed compromise)
- Committed Capacity Unit (CCU): 1 CCU = 1 reserved GPU-hour within the customer's dedicated pool. For measurement and cross-model parity we normalize each CCU to a "reference GPU" that is defined in the glossary (commit-glossary-v1.md). Customers may request the mapping table for specific model families.
- Committed Throughput: the sum across the pool of successfully emitted tokens divided by time, computed as the 5-minute rolling average and reported as tokens/sec normalized to the reference GPU. Measurement excludes scheduled maintenance windows (customer-notified > 48 hours) and Redwood-initiated unavoidable maintenance (with a 4-hr notification window).

2) Credit ladder (proposed)
- If realized throughput >= 95% of committed: no credit.
- If realized throughput >= 90% and < 95%: 5% credit of monthly committed fee.
- If realized throughput >= 80% and < 90%: 12% credit.
- If realized throughput < 80%: 25% credit, capped at 45% per month.

Rationale: this keeps an escalating but bounded exposure and avoids outsized credits for short transient dips. Credits are applied to the following billing cycle and are the sole financial remedy (no termination or additional damages).

3) Measurement transparency
- Redwood will deliver a monthly throughput report (CSV export) and a one-time export on request for audits (subject to a standard request SLA).

Next actions:
- Aditya: can you confirm Lumina's initial CCU sizing (estimate from your team) by Tue 24 Mar?
- Elena: if the ladder above is acceptable, we will incorporate the language into a clean contract for DocuSign signature and provide a redline to the Lumina document.

Thanks — attaching commit-glossary-v1.md for reference.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

Attachment: commit-glossary-v1.md

From: Elena Park <elena@luminadx.com>

1) Can Redwood include one sample monthly throughput CSV (sanitized) so our SREs can validate the export format?
2) Please add explicit language that warm-up traffic (first 10 minutes after pool scale events) is excluded from monthly measurements.

If you can add those two bullets to the clean contract, procurement will route to DocuSign and we should be able to sign by the end of next week.

Action items agreed:
- Redwood to deliver sanitized sample CSV + updated clean contract with warm-up exclusion
- Lumina to confirm CCU sizing (internal) and return the clean contract for signature

I'll wait for the updated doc and the DocuSign link.
